content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Construct a cumulative frequency table from grouped data
Use the graph to estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range
Read values from a cumulative frequency graph
Interpret percentiles and other statistics from the graph
Cumulative frequency tells us how many values are
a given value. By plotting a cumulative frequency graph, we can visually estimate the median, quartiles, and interquartile range without doing complex calculations.
This technique is widely used in exam analysis -- for example, finding the mark at which 75% of students scored below, or determining how many students achieved above a certain grade boundary.
Explore cumulative frequency — build cumulative frequency diagrams and read off quartiles using the interactive visualisation below.
is a running total of frequencies. For each class interval, it tells us the total number of values up to and including that class.
$$\text{Cumulative frequency} = \text{sum of all frequencies up to that class}$$
